About the Studio

Studio Forma is a boutique architectural planning and interior design studio, guiding every project from the first idea to the final detail. We believe a good space is one that truly serves the life lived in it - functional, precise, and inspiring every day.

faqs.question: How long does an average design process take?
faqs.answer: A home styling project usually takes between 4 to 8 weeks, while planning and redesigning a full apartment ranges from 3 to 6 months.

faqs.question: Do you work with your own suppliers and tradespeople?
faqs.answer: Yes, we have a network of leading tradespeople (carpenters, electricians, contractors) who work with us in full collaboration, but we're also happy to work with your own suppliers.

faqs.question: How is the project budget determined?
faqs.answer: At our first introductory meeting we define a clear budget framework. Every material and furniture choice is then made to fully match the budget set in advance.

blog.author: Maya Segev, Lead Interior Designer
blog.title: 5 Lighting Mistakes Everyone Makes in Living Room Design

meta.description: The right lighting can make a space feel bigger and completely transform its mood. Here's what you need to know before choosing light fixtures.
meta.title: 5 Lighting Mistakes Everyone Makes in Living Room Design

children.text: This article's content was written for demo purposes only, as part of a sample site built with Payload CMS.
The right lighting can make a space feel bigger and completely transform its mood. Here's what you need to know before choosing light fixtures.
Lighting is one of the most influential elements in how a home feels, yet many leave it until the very end of the process - and that's exactly the first mistake.
1. Relying on a Single Light Source
A single fixture in the middle of the ceiling creates harsh shadows and a flat feeling. Combining ambient, task, and decorative lighting is what gives a living room depth and character.
2. Inconsistent Color Temperature
Mixing warm and cool bulbs in the same space creates visual discomfort. We always recommend staying within the same color temperature (typically 2700K-3000K) across every fixture in the room.
3. No Dimming (or the Wrong Kind)
Proper dimming lets you match the mood to the time of day and how the space is used. Installing quality dimmers at the planning stage saves a major headache later on.

blog.author: Maya Segev, Lead Interior Designer
blog.title: How to Choose Kitchen Materials That Last for Years

meta.description: From natural stone to porcelain granite surfaces - a comprehensive look at durability, maintenance, and design for the modern kitchen.
meta.title: How to Choose Kitchen Materials That Last for Years

children.text: This article's content was written for demo purposes only, as part of a sample site built with Payload CMS.
From natural stone to porcelain granite surfaces - a comprehensive look at durability, maintenance, and design for the modern kitchen.
The kitchen is the heart of the home, and the materials you choose need to withstand tough daily use alongside a luxurious look.
Natural Stone
Marble offers a unique, luxurious look with no two slabs alike, but it's relatively porous and needs periodic sealing to prevent staining from oil, wine, and acids.
Porcelain Granite
Porcelain surfaces resist scratches, heat, and stains almost completely, and now come in patterns that convincingly mimic marble - a great combination of aesthetics and low maintenance.
Quartz (Engineered Stone)
Quartz offers high durability and uniform color, suiting kitchens that want a combination of luxury and simple, long-lasting maintenance.

comments.body: The principle of planning circulation before choosing furniture is so obvious once you hear it, but nobody thinks of it upfront. Great insight.

blog.author: Daniel Or, Principal Architect
blog.title: 3 Principles for Open-Space Planning That Actually Works

meta.description: An open floor plan isn't just about removing a wall - it's precise planning of movement, function, and lighting working together.
meta.title: 3 Principles for Open-Space Planning That Actually Works

children.text: This article's content was written for demo purposes only, as part of a sample site built with Payload CMS.
An open floor plan isn't just about removing a wall - it's precise planning of movement, function, and lighting working together.
1. Visual Separation Without Walls
Furniture, rugs, and subtle ceiling height changes can define "rooms" within an open space, without giving up the sense of flow and air.
2. Consistent Materials and Lighting
When every zone in the space speaks the same material language and color temperature, the transition between the seating area, dining area, and kitchen feels natural and planned.
3. Planning Circulation First

Before choosing furniture, it's important to map the natural "walking paths" through the space - that's ultimately what determines whether a home feels spacious or cramped, even in a relatively small apartment.
